hook: AI gave you a 47-step plan when you asked for help with one email. You're not broken. AI just doesn't know you yet.
caption:
AI gave you a 47-step plan when you asked for help with one email. You're not broken. AI just doesn't know you yet.

Here's what's actually happening:

AI defaults to the most comprehensive answer possible because it has no idea if you're a first-timer or a pro. It doesn't know if you want bullet points or prose. It doesn't know you hate corporate softening language. It doesn't know you'd rather have three options than one "perfect" answer.

So it hedges. It covers everything. It writes like it's explaining to everyone at once.

Which means it's really explaining to no one.

The fix isn't prompting harder. It's not adding "be concise" at the end of every message and hoping for the best.

The fix is AI that already knows:
— You think in systems, not steps
— You want the sharp version, not the diplomatic one
— You process by talking it out, not reading a wall of text

That's what a BootFile does. It's a profile built around how YOUR brain actually works — so AI stops responding to the average person and starts responding to you.

One setup. Every conversation after that, calibrated.
